summary: Created mcp-server/tests/gui/config-helpers.test.ts with 44 test cases covering mrDeriveSlug (12 cases), mrValidateSlug (13 cases), mrHasChanges (11 cases), and pmCloneAssignments (8 cases). Used the @vitest-environment jsdom + vm.runInThisContext() loading approach — consistent with the existing test pattern in client-rendering.test.ts and project-detail-helpers.test.ts — to evaluate the vanilla JS files in the jsdom globalThis scope, making their global-scope functions accessible without a module system. Module-level globals (mrModels, mrOriginal) are manipulated directly on globalThis in beforeEach to isolate mrHasChanges test state. Minimal stubs provided for API and configDirty; escapeHtml and UI are supplied by the shared setup-gui-globals.ts setup file. All 44 new tests pass; full suite of 3593 tests across 118 files passes with zero regressions.

comments.note: config-model-registry.js and config-persona-models.js have no top-level IIFE or registration hooks, which makes vm.runInThisContext() loading clean. However, the module-level vars (mrModels, mrOriginal, pmAssignments, etc.) are global state that leaks between any tests loading these files in the same jsdom context. The beforeEach reset pattern used here is correct, but future test authors loading these files must be aware of this shared-global hazard. A comment in setup-gui-globals.ts documenting which globals are 'owned' by each view module would reduce future confusion.

comments.note: mrHasChanges uses index-based comparison (position i in mrModels vs position i in mrOriginal). Reordering models without content changes will falsely report true. This is documented in the source code comment and is by design (mirrors save order). The test suite does not cover a reorder-only scenario — low risk since the UI has no drag-to-reorder feature currently.

mrValidateSlug('   ') (whitespace-only string) passes the !slug falsy check (non-empty string is truthy) and returns the generic 'lowercase alphanumeric' error rather than 'Slug is required.' UX is slightly misleading but functionally correct — the slug is rejected. Not covered by tests, low impact.

No test for purely numeric slug (e.g. mrDeriveSlug('123') → '123', mrValidateSlug('123') → ''). Both functions handle it correctly per the MR_SLUG_REGEX rule, which explicitly allows [a-z0-9]. Benign gap.

summary: Code review PASS. The test file config-helpers.test.ts is well-structured, consistent with existing GUI test patterns, and achieves solid coverage of all four pure helpers. Loading strategy (vm.runInThisContext in beforeAll) is correct and matches the established client-rendering.test.ts and project-detail-helpers.test.ts pattern. Global state management for mrHasChanges (beforeEach reset) is the right isolation approach for shared module-level vars. The existence-guarded stubs for API and configDirty prevent double-registration conflicts. Assertion quality is appropriate — toContain('lowercase alphanumeric') for format error messages, exact string matches for required/reserved error messages, and proper clone-isolation assertions for pmCloneAssignments. No blocking issues found. One documentation-forward item tagged for setup-gui-globals.ts to document which globals are owned by each view module.

comments.note: The mrValidateSlug assertions for format errors use toContain('lowercase alphanumeric') rather than asserting the full message. This is intentional and defensible — partial matching decouples tests from exact wording. However, a follow-up improvement would be to export or document the exact error message strings as named constants in the source file, making tests (and user-facing copy) easier to maintain if the wording changes.

The test for 'returns false when mrModels is null but mrOriginal is set' correctly sets globalThis.mrOriginal in beforeEach and then explicitly sets mrOriginal to a value, relying on the fact that var declarations at top level in vm.runInThisContext become globalThis properties. This is correct, but future test authors may not understand why setting globalThis.mrModels affects the function's internal mrModels binding. A single inline comment noting 'var mrModels in the JS source IS globalThis.mrModels in vm.runInThisContext context' would prevent confusion.

[documentation-forward] setup-gui-globals.ts lacks a comment documenting which globals are 'owned' by each view module (e.g. mrModels, mrOriginal, mrEditingId owned by config-model-registry.js; pmModels, pmAssignments, pmOriginal etc. owned by config-persona-models.js). Future test authors loading multiple view modules in the same jsdom context need this ownership map to avoid global collision bugs. Add a brief comment to setup-gui-globals.ts or a linked note in the GUI test README.
